# `nebulaos-osconfig` helper reference

Every OS setting a printer has is read and written here. The [API reference](MOONRAKER-API.md) stops at the endpoint; this page picks up where it stops.

Source: `NebulaOS-firmware` at `b95b156`, `scripts/build/overlay/usr/lib/nebulaos/python/nebulaos_osconfig/`. **18 modules.**

## The contract

`nebulaos-osconfig` is a command-line program: **argv in, one JSON object out.** It is run by the Moonraker component as a subprocess, which is the whole reason the privilege boundary works - the component never writes a system file itself.

```
nebulaos-osconfig DOMAIN VERB [--option value]...
```

It prints `{"ok": true, ...}` merged with the helper's own result, or `{"ok": false, "error": "<CODE>", "message": "..."}`, and never a traceback - the dispatcher catches every exception and turns it into that contract. Read-only verbs are listed in `cli.py`'s `READ_ONLY` set and are the only ones that skip the audit log; every change writes one line to the persistent system log.

## How to read the tables

**Reached by** is the `DOMAIN VERB` that routes to the function, taken from the dispatcher rather than from the function's name. A function with nothing there is not reachable from the command line: it is used by another module, by a boot service, or by a test.

**Result keys** are the keys that function's own `return` statements carry, extracted with `ast`. A blank means the returns could not be read - not that the function returns nothing.

**No module here is hardware-verified.** Everything is read from source.

## `camera.py`

nebulaos_osconfig.camera - Creality Nebula Camera controls (G121, Run 22, The owner's list
2026-10-28; investigation _scratch/run22/G121-nebulacam-investigation.md). camera status
stored settings, defaults, the camera camera set --json '{...}'        change some settings
(saved, then applied) camera defaults                  every setting back to the camera's
defaults camera reset                     reboot the camera (XU selector 17) camera version
the camera's firmware string (XU selector 15) camera apply [--device DEV]      re-apply
everything (S50webcam, when the camera appears - nothing persists in it) The camera (USB
a108:2231, uvcvideo) keeps nothing over a reboot, power cycle or USB re-enumeration, so the
settings live here (camera/camera.json, atomic) and are applied again each time it appears.
Apply order (one control per ioctl): auto switches, manual values, the rest, then the IR mode.
Exposure is one-way: the camera reads auto_exposure 0 (its own auto mode) but only accepts 1
(manual); the way back is a camera reset, which clears the stored manual flag BEFORE the reboot
so the re-apply cannot switch it on. The vendor Extension Unit (GUID
41769ea2-04de-e347-8b2b-f4341aff003b, found in the USB descriptors, not assumed to be unit 6)
is used ONLY through a frozen allow-list of (selector, query) pairs. Selector 13 (firmware
update mode: the camera turns into a mass-storage device) is not in it and cannot be sent: no
command-line or HTTP parameter carries a selector number. Flip stays in Mainsail. Gamma, hue,
backlight compensation and focus (fixed lens) are never written.

## `cleanup.py`

nebulaos_osconfig.cleanup - storage overview and "Clean up Creality files" (G66, 2026-10-16;
architecture review 2026-10-16 followed). The data drive (/usr/data) is shared: NebulaOS keeps
everything in /usr/data/nebulaos plus the print files in /usr/data/printer_data/gcodes; the
Creality system (and the community helper script's add-ons for it) keep their data next to it.
"Clean up Creality files" removes that data from a FIXED list - never "everything else" - with
these guards: - /usr/data/printer_data/gcodes (NebulaOS's print files, the USB stick mount
below it) is never touched; of printer_data only the other entries go - nothing that is, or
contains, a mount point; symlinks are removed as links, never followed; nothing outside
/usr/data - the swap file only when it is not in use - Creality's timelapse videos only when
asked for - refused while printing (the Moonraker component checks first) - the print
statistics a later import reads (Run 23, 2026-11-02): Creality's lifetime print counter and
print history, and the old Moonraker database (printer_data/database) - see STATISTICS_KEEP
Everything not on the list stays: macaddr.txt, wpa_supplicant.conf, factory_test_result,
.nebulaos-clean-reset*, .keep, nebulaos*, ... Whatever the other slot runs is allowed; when it
is Creality the screen says plainly that it will stop working.

## `image.py`

nebulaos_osconfig.image - install a system image (NebulaOS or Creality .img) into the slot that
is NOT running, from the touchscreen (on-printer image updates, human decisions 2026-10-14): -
NebulaOS may occupy both A/B slots; an install always writes the inactive slot (kernel +
rootfs) and then switches the OTA marker to it. The running slot is never written. The RTOS
partitions are never written. - Sources: USB sticks, config/firmware/os (Mainsail upload) and
the image `ota download` fetched (G79, Run 23; sha256 checked against the release). - Integrity
checks only (no signing): the Creality OTA envelope (7z, the chained per-chunk MD5 scheme,
declared sizes and MD5s), a MIPS uImage kernel and a squashfs rootfs that fit their partitions,
and a read-back of the written partitions. - Older versions may be installed. Creality images
are accepted. - One automatic fallback after an install: the new slot boots as a trial;
S99nebulaos-image-trial confirms it, or switches back once. - G91 (2026-10-22): refused at the
request while the printer is busy (common.busy_state, request profile - a pending trial of the
running slot counts), under the one maintenance lock. Two stop points instead of G88's "wait
for the print": before the marker write (stop, blank the written slot) and after it, before the
reboot (marker back, read back, TRIAL deleted, slot blanked; if the marker cannot be put back,
nothing more is touched and the new system starts at the next power-on). The trial verdict
waits while a print runs. A slot confirms itself by its first passed trial: system/slot-
confirmed-<slot>, keyed on the slot's uImage header (name + CRCs) and squashfs superblock,
deleted when an install starts writing that slot. Every switch into an unconfirmed slot writes
a TRIAL record (system.swap_slot). image list                      .img files from the sources
image check --file ID           open the package, report what it holds image install --file ID
--sha256 HEX   start the install (background job) image status                    the
running/last job, slots, last result image ack                       the screen showed the last
result The format is the one scripts/package/build-img.py writes and Creality's own updater
reads: an encrypted 7z holding <top>/ota_v<ver>/ with ota_update.in, and per payload
<name>.NNNN.<md5 of the previous chunk, or of the whole payload for chunk 0000> plus
ota_md5_<name>.<md5> listing the chunk MD5s.

"plug in USB, pick a compiled .bin, flash - no Creality bootloader knowledge needed". status

media.sh) and the built-in NebulaOS firmware; each one checked offline flash    one file, by id
and the sha256 the user confirmed Flashing is NOT reimplemented here. The file is checked and
prepared (mcu_image.prepare(): a raw NebulaOS-klipper-mcu build is packed into the Creality
format), snapshotted to tmpfs so a pulled USB stick or a new upload cannot change it mid-
flight, and handed to the existing CLI, `nebulaos-mcu flash <file>`, which refuses while
printing, stops Klipper, runs mcu_flash_file.py (bootloader entry, hardware-id allow-list,
transfer, app start) and restarts Klipper whatever happened.

## `ota.py`

nebulaos_osconfig.ota - NebulaOS system updates over the internet (G79). Design:
_scratch/run15/G79-ota-design.md; 2026-10-29 (Run 23): NO signing key - the printer downloads
only over HTTPS from github.com and checks the size and sha256 listed in the release record.
ota status                 the last check and the download (read-only) ota check [--force]
ask the release channel whether a newer NebulaOS is published (at most once per 24 h unless
forced; never while the printer is busy) ota download               fetch the offered .img
(background job) into the "ota" image source; the install is then the ordinary `image install
--file ota/<name>` (busy refusal, stop points, trial, rollback) ota discard
delete the downloaded image Trust: the stable channel is the latest GitHub release of NebulaOS-
KE/NebulaOS. Every request is HTTPS with certificate checks (the image's CA bundle), to
github.com / api.github.com and, through redirects, only to GitHub's release asset hosts. The
release record nebulaos-release.json (tools/release/ make-release-record.py) names the image,
its size and sha256; the image is kept only when both match. TLS needs a set clock: before
CLOCK_FLOOR nothing is fetched.

## `poweronlogo.py`

nebulaos_osconfig.poweronlogo - the power-on logo: the picture the RTOS (zero.bin, in the
running slot's rtos/rtos2 partition) draws before Linux starts. G58/G40 (human design,
2026-10-15): - always a logo, NebulaOS's by default; the only choice is an image the user
uploaded to the boot logo folder (the same one becomes the Linux boot screen, bootdisplay.py);
- "Set NebulaOS logo" when the original logo is still in the RTOS; - "Restore Creality logo" -
the original, saved on the printer before the first change (or copied from the other slot's
RTOS, which still has it); - the running slot's RTOS, A or B: slot A too once it holds NebulaOS
(G40). Only the logo slot inside zero.bin is written (rtos_logo.py: 480x272 baseline JPEG,
4:2:0, at most 10899 bytes at 0x5e50c). Before a write the whole image outside that slot must
hash to FRAME_SHA256 - the stock image with the slot zeroed, the same for every logo - so an
RTOS that is not the known one is never touched. Every write is read back. The Moonraker
component refuses all of this while printing.

| Function | Reached by | Result keys |
|---|---|---|
| `check_writable()` | - | - |
| `classify(image)` | - | - |
| `convert(path)` | - | - |
| `nebulaos_slot_bytes()` | - | - |
| `restore_original()` | - | `applies`, `logo`, `result`, `slot` |
| `set_custom(path)` | - | `applies`, `logo`, `quality`, `result`, `slot` |
| `set_nebulaos()` | - | `applies`, `logo`, `result`, `slot` |
| `status()` | - | `logo`, `original_available`, `reason`, `slot`, `writable` |
| `write_slot(slot_bytes)` | - | `applies`, `logo`, `result`, `slot` |

## `snapshot.py`

nebulaos_osconfig.snapshot - copies of the user's settings (G65, 2026-10-16).
config/backups/settings-<UTC>-<reason>/   visible in Mainsail printer.cfg moonraker.conf
songs.conf    (calibration is in printer.cfg) macros/  nebulascreen/nebulascreen.json
calibration/ SNAPSHOT.txt                             what, why, which system, and where the
database copy is Moonraker's database (Mainsail's settings - and login data and API keys, so
never under config, which Mainsail can download): --db file   copied straight from
printer_data/database (S04, before Moonraker starts - a consistent copy) into system/settings-
db/<snapshot name>/ --db api    Moonraker's own POST /server/database/backup, which writes
printer_data/backup/database/<snapshot name>.db (Moonraker refuses while printing - recorded,
not hidden) When: at the first boot of every new or rolled-back system (S04, before any
migration touches a setting) and from the housekeeping loop whenever the settings changed since
the newest snapshot - so the newest copy always predates the next update (Moonraker updates
components without a hook). The newest KEEP are kept, with their database copies.

| Function | Reached by | Result keys |
|---|---|---|
| `fingerprint()` | - | - |
| `prune(keep)` | - | - |
| `snapshots()` | - | - |
| `status()` | `settings status` | `keep`, `snapshots` |
| `take(reason, db, if_changed, now)` | `settings snapshot` | `database`, `files`, `name`, `newest`, `pruned`, `result` |

## `spoolman.py`

nebulaos_osconfig.spoolman - the Spoolman server Moonraker talks to (G125, Run 22, 2026-10-28:
Settings > Connections > Spoolman on the screen, the same layout as the printer entry).
spoolman status                          {configured, server, host, port} spoolman set --host
HOST --port PORT     [spoolman] server: http://HOST:PORT spoolman remove
the [spoolman] section goes The setting lives where a user would put it by hand: the [spoolman]
section of the user's moonraker.conf (config root, editable in Mainsail). Only that section's
`server` line is touched - every other line, comment and option (sync_rate, ...) stays as it
is; the file is written atomically. Not an [include]: Moonraker refuses to start on an include
that matches no file. Moonraker reads it only at start: a change returns restart: "moonraker"
and the caller restarts it (machine.services.restart moonraker, like the hostname). Refused
while the printer is busy (G91 maintenance lock + request profile).

| Function | Reached by | Result keys |
|---|---|---|
| `remove()` | `spoolman remove` | `configured`, `host`, `port`, `restart`, `result`, `server` |
| `set_server(host, port)` | `spoolman set` | `configured`, `host`, `port`, `restart`, `result`, `server` |
| `status()` | `spoolman status` | `configured`, `host`, `port`, `server` |

## `stats.py`

nebulaos_osconfig.stats - print statistics from before NebulaOS (Run 23, 2026-11-02: Settings >
Printer > Statistics). stats baseline     what the printer printed before NebulaOS, imported
once NebulaOS counts its own prints with Moonraker's history (on by default; the NebulaOS
Moonraker component adds them up). What came before lives on the data drive, next to NebulaOS,
and is read here - never written: creality   Creality's lifetime print time:
/usr/data/creality/userdata/ config/user_data_not_deleted.json, kept by Creality's master-
server (stock 1.1.0.12: "total_time" in seconds, the sum of Klipper's
print_stats.print_duration per print). The file is base64 of AES-128-CBC, zero-padded; key and
IV are two 16-character strings in master-server (stock 1.1.0.12, offsets 0xc85e8 and 0xc862c),
found against ke-dev's own counter (Run 23): '{ "total_time": 468971, "creality_num": 1 }'.
With it userdata/history/print_history_record.json (plain JSON, the prints Creality still
lists): count and filament. moonraker  an earlier Moonraker's history (OpenKE, helper script):
/usr/data/printer_data/database/moonraker-sql.db, tables job_totals and job_history
(Moonraker's own schema). A source is imported once and then kept in /usr/data/nebulaos/system/
stats-baseline.json, so its numbers survive "Clean up Creality files" or a reinstall of
Creality's system. A source that is absent or unreadable is looked at again next time. "Clean
up Creality files" keeps both sources (cleanup.STATISTICS_KEEP, printer_data/database).

| Function | Reached by | Result keys |
|---|---|---|
| `baseline()` | `stats baseline` | `sources` |
| `decrypt_creality(blob, key_hex, iv_hex)` | - | - |
| `read_creality_counter()` | - | - |
| `read_creality_history()` | - | - |
| `read_old_moonraker()` | - | `by_status`, `filament_mm`, `job_time`, `jobs`, `longest_print`, `print_time`, `reason`, `since`, `status` |

## `updates.py`

nebulaos_osconfig.updates - G73 (2026-10-17): is a pending app update installable on this
printer? Moonraker's update_manager installs Klipper and Moonraker updates with `pip install -U
-r <requirements>` against the NebulaOS package index (ready-made packages only - there is no
compiler on the printer), and a Klipper update that changes klippy/chelper also needs a
matching c_helper.so (G72). When the index has not caught up yet (it builds daily), the update
fails and is rolled back. This check says so BEFORE the update button is pressed. Advisory
only: it never blocks an update. readiness         the last result (read-only, cached file)
check-readiness   run the check now and store it [--if-changed] Rules (architecture review
2026-10-17): - the target commit is Moonraker's own remote_hash; no ref guessing - no `git
fetch` and no other write to the app repositories (Moonraker owns fetching) - only `git show
<remote_hash>:<file>` / ls-tree - never started while update_manager is busy (pip in the same
venv) or printing; an update started DURING a check overlaps it (pip --dry-run only reads the
venv), which is accepted - read-only git: show, ls-tree, cat-file - never fetch - pip runs as
Moonraker runs it: the app's own venv, `--dry-run`, the index from /etc/pip.conf, temporary
files on /usr/data (not RAM)

| Function | Reached by | Result keys |
|---|---|---|
| `check(if_changed)` | `updates check-readiness` | `apps`, `checked_at`, `checked_epoch`, `message`, `result`, `targets` |
| `readiness()` | `updates readiness` | - |

## `wifi.py`

nebulaos_osconfig.wifi - Wi-Fi networks for wlan0 through wpa_supplicant's control socket (Q3,
2026-10-11). Replaces GuppyScreen's direct socket use: the GUI and Mainsail both go through
machine.nebulaos.wifi.*. status    association state and the saved networks scan      a fresh
scan (waits for the results) connect   {"ssid", "password"} on stdin - never on a command line.
A new network is only saved once it has connected; a wrong password or a timeout removes it
again and returns to the previous one forget    remove every saved entry for an SSID
wpa_supplicant owns /usr/data/nebulaos/network/wpa_supplicant.conf (update_config=1,
SAVE_CONFIG). The passphrase is turned into the 64-hex WPA PSK here, so it is never stored in
plain text and never quoted into a control command. SSIDs are sent hex-encoded for the same
reason.

|---|---|---|
